judged_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:641-654 — `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` (an association-level delete that executes immediately against the join table) and then separately calls `group.save`, but `group.save` persists unrelated attributes (`name`, `alias_level`, `visible`) loaded into the same `group` object at the top of the action; if a concurrent request has updated one of those attributes on the group's `name`/`visible`/`alias_level` between this action's `Group.find` and its `save`, the stale in-memory `group` object here overwrites the concurrent change with its own stale values (last-writer-wins), because there is no optimistic locking (`lock_version`) or transaction wrapping the read-modify-write span from `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` to `group.save`. Rebuttal: the window is narrow and the fields involved are low-frequency admin edits, so real-world collision is rare — reported at reduced confidence for that reason. Confidence 55, severity P3.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `group.save`, but it never modifies `group.name/visible/alias_level` inside this action. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `save` only issues an UPDATE for dirty (changed) attributes; deleting from the `users` association does not mark those scalar group attributes as changed, so `group.save` will not persist stale `name`/`visible`/`alias_level` values back to the DB in the “last-writer-wins” way described. The alleged overwrite window/optimistic locking concern is therefore not supported by what’s shown in the diff.
